programme: TET1 (TET-family 5mC→5hmC demethylase) and CEBPB (C/EBP-family bZIP transcription factor) jointly reshape methylation/transcription state at differentiation-controlling loci — TET1 opening chromatin by active demethylation, CEBPB then driving transcriptional activation of the newly accessible programme.
role_in_a: In MS, TET1 supports oligodendrocyte generation/maturation and tracks the altered methylation landscape of chronic inactive demyelinated lesions; CEBPB sits within the differential DNA-methylation signature that distinguishes MS from other demyelinating diseases (NMO). Together they point to disrupted epigenetic control of glial differentiation as part of the failure to remyelinate.
role_in_b: In gastric cancer, TET1-linked methylation change marks malignant transformation and is exploited as a cfDNA blood-based early-detection signature; CEBPB actively drives gastric epithelial cell plasticity (an EMT-like dedifferentiation) that promotes liver metastasis. Together they point to the same demethylation-then-transcription logic being repurposed to drive tumour cell-state change and spread.
shared_axis: Both diseases are, at the cellular level, problems of a differentiation-state switch failing or being hijacked — oligodendrocyte precursors not completing maturation in MS lesions, gastric epithelial cells dedifferentiating toward an invasive phenotype in cancer — and TET1-mediated demethylation paired with CEBPB-driven transcription is the epigenetic machinery independently implicated in each switch, even though no source here states the two diseases share this axis.
reasoning: TET1 and CEBPB are each placed by name in both diseases by retrieved papers, not just by recurrence, and their pairing (demethylase plus bZIP activator) is a nameable, generic epigenetic-reprogramming logic. But no paper ties MS and gastric cancer together through this axis, CEBPB is flagged discordant across patient groups (its role differs in specifics between the diseases — methylation marker vs. active driver — rather than an identical mechanism), and 9 of the other 10 listed factors have reader-confirmed off-topic or absent literature, so the account rests on two factors, not the full set.
support: PMID 39770028 — TET1 promotes oligodendrocyte generation (MS); PMID 37286732 — TET1 in epigenomic/transcriptomic profiling of chronic inactive demyelination (MS); PMID 42452430 — CEBPB within DNA-methylation signatures distinguishing MS/NMO from other conditions (MS); PMID 41359088 — TET1-linked cfDNA methylation signature for early gastric cancer detection; PMID 41916135 — TET1-linked dose-dependent DNA methylation change in a gastric-cancer context, mechanism unclear from the title alone; PMID 41836678 — CEBPB-regulated gastric cell plasticity promotes liver metastasis of gastric cancer, direct and mechanistic.
how_to_falsify: Inhibit or knock down TET1 (or use a catalytically dead mutant) in an oligodendrocyte precursor differentiation assay and separately in the CEBPB-driven gastric cell-plasticity/liver-metastasis model from PMID 41836678; if TET1 loss fails to blunt CEBPB target-gene activation or the associated cell-state transition in either system, the proposed shared demethylase-plus-CEBPB axis is not operative.
caveats: Brain and stomach are developmentally unrelated tissues, and tissue-generic factors common to both (EBF1, TCF4, SOX10, NR5A2, PAX5, DLX5, NR3C1, STAT4, TAL1, ZEB2, HDAC7, SREBF1) were already stripped before ranking, so this is not simple shared-tissue noise. TET1 and CEBPB are each supported in only 265/780 (34%) of comparisons — mid-pack, not the strongest recurring factors (EBF2 at 328/780 and HLX at 289/780 recur more but have no relevant literature per the reader's notes, so recurrence and mechanistic relevance are not aligned here). CEBPB is marked 'discordant' while TET1 is 'concordant' — treat CEBPB as a same-family, different-role echo, not an identical mechanism. SOX6 also has one paper per disease (40858115 for MS, 31726103 for gastric cancer) but its actual network targets (COL2A1, COMP, MATN1, PTHLH, RUNX2) form a chondrogenic/cartilage regulon, not an oligodendrocyte or gastric-epithelial one, so it was excluded from the carrying set as a likely mismatch. HEYL, ZNF300 and INSM1 each have real gastric-cancer literature but zero MS evidence, so they support a stomach-cancer-only story. EBF2, HLX, ZNF354C, ATOH8, MLXIPL and TCFL5 have no disease-specific support per the reader's notes despite meeting the recurrence threshold. The 780 comparisons derive from only 3 independent cohort pairs, not 780 independent observations.
